Your gothic metal mix sounds this thin.

Hollow. Then it flips, and the guitars finally have a floor under them. That's 2.6 dB more between 160 and 315 Hz. No extra width, no tricks. I'd rather fix the weight than fake the size, and at doom tempo you hear every bit of it.

Level goes from -17.9 to -10.6 LUFS on the way. It's Velvet Requiem by Vesper Mortis.

What did you hear first, the low mids or the level?

An eight-string in standard F# puts the open low string at 46 Hz.

→ That is the same octave as the bass guitar and the kick fundamental, which usually sits somewhere around 50 to 80 Hz in modern metal.
→ On a stereo file, any low cut or shelf at the master hits all three at once. Pull the guitar mud and the kick goes thin.
→ With stems, the guitar low end gets its own dynamic EQ and the kick keeps its attack.
→ Palm-muted chugs are transients. Heavy bus limiting flattens the exact rhythm that defines djent.

Eight-string players: cut the low mud in the mix or leave it for the master?

Same room. Same monitors. Same listening level.

→ Hearing is not linear. The equal-loudness contours (ISO 226) show that lows and highs seem weaker at lower volume.
→ Turn the monitors up and a mix suddenly feels fuller, even though nothing in the file changed.
→ So every session runs at one fixed, calibrated level, and EQ decisions don't drift with the volume knob.
→ Version comparisons are loudness-matched for the same reason.

Lights low. Meters on. Then we listen.

Your black metal mix sounds this thin. I flipped it against the release master so you can hear exactly where.

▸ Width. I put 2.7 dB more into the sides, so the tremolo wall wraps around the vocals instead of sitting on them.
▸ Body. 160 to 630 Hz comes up 3 to 4 dB. That's where your riffs went missing.
▸ Level. -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP. Streaming turns you down to about there anyway, so I don't push past it.

It's Frostbound Sepulchre by Vesper Mortis. Out in January.

What did you hear first, the width or the low mids?

Your gothic metal mix: -18 LUFS.

That's where it starts. Quiet, and a bit hollow. You'll notice it when it flips: I brought 160 to 315 Hz up by 2.3 dB, and the whole song lands at -10.4 LUFS. I didn't widen it. Didn't need to, because the room was already there in your mix and I'd only have smeared it.

It's Velvet Requiem by Vesper Mortis.

Your death metal mix sounds this thin. You'll hear it the second it flips.

I didn't touch the arrangement. I lifted 160 to 315 Hz by 2.5 dB, because that's where a death metal riff gets its weight, and I gave the sides 2.5 dB more room. Then it went from -17.4 to -8.8 LUFS. That's all.

It's Carrion Liturgy by Vesper Mortis.
